human_tolerance.notes: Forest-edge, second-growth and open-canopy deciduous woodland specialist; Wikipedia says it avoids non-forested agricultural land. Judgement from the habitat description.

phases.name: absent
phases.note: US curve (GBIF) is at or below 0.01 of its peak Nov-Mar; the birds winter in Central America and the Caribbean.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Authored window: the US curve peaks May-Sep and Wikipedia gives breeding in southern Canada and the eastern US, but no published month dates were found.

vocalizations.description: A series of musical see-see-see notes (Wikipedia). Season and cooldown are judgement.
A soft chip note (Wikipedia). Used as the alarm call in the program: judgement, the source does not give its function.

taxonomy.note: GBIF species/match returned usageKey 2489985, ACCEPTED, SPECIES, Setophaga ruticilla (Linnaeus, 1758); iNaturalist taxon 10247 is active at species rank.

external.note: iNaturalist 10247 and eBird amered from Wikidata P3151 and P3444; ITIS 182949 from Wikidata P685.

range.note: Breeding in southern Canada and the eastern US; wintering in Central America (BZ, GT, HN, SV, NI, CR, PA) and the West Indies (JM named for elevation). Country codes derived from these named regions; no introduced populations listed.

traits.nest_type.note: Neat cup-shaped nest in the lower part of a bush.

traits.mass_kg.note: The mass column is 8.24 g in both Setophaga ruticilla rows of the CC0 dataset. Wikipedia sex and season means (6.9-8.7 g) agree.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: Min and max of the Wikipedia sex-and-season mean masses: 6.9 g (female, winter) to 8.7 g (female, summer).

traits.length_m.note: Midpoint of the 11-14 cm total length range.

traits.wingspan_m.note: Midpoint of the 16-23 cm wingspan range.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Mean lifespan under a constant annual hazard: -1/ln(s) with s the mean of the two Setophaga ruticilla apparent-survival rows (0.55 and 0.522, mean 0.536), giving 1.60 y. Single-row values are 1.67 y (Canada, mark-resight) and 1.54 y (US, MAPS). Limitations: apparent survival underestimates true survival where birds emigrate; first-year mortality is not modelled; this is a mean, not a median (about 1.1 y); two studies only. Not a maximum or captive value; Wikipedia's banded-bird maximum of over 10 years is not used.

traits.diet.note: Authored allocation. Wikipedia says the redstart feeds almost exclusively on insects and that few berries and seeds are eaten: invertebrate 0.95, fruit 0.05.

traits.social.note: Territorial, mostly monogamous pairs in the breeding season. Solitary with group size 1-2 follows the robin convention; judgement.

traits.activity_pattern.note: Feeds by day through flycatching and gleaning; no night activity described.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Flight (flycatching and foraging sallies) is described. Ground hopping is judgement, not described in the source.

traits.defense.note: Judgement: flees to cover, like other small perching passerines.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement; no source gives a wariness scale. Set between the robin (0.2) and the more skittish species.

habitat.use.note: Judgement from 'found feeding in the mid to lower regions of a tree or shrub'.

habitat.resources.note: Insects by flycatching and gleaning; few berries (barberry, serviceberry, magnolia); cup nests in the lower part of a bush; shrubs and perches. Weights and the nest_cup month window are judgement.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Habitat description (open-canopy deciduous forest, second growth, edges; avoids non-forested agricultural land) supports Avoider; judgement.

seasonal.strategy.note: Both survival rows are coded migrant in the CC0 dataset. Wikipedia says the species is migratory and winters in the tropics.

seasonal.phases.note: Absent window derived from the US GBIF curve (near zero Nov-Mar). The breeding window is authored; the curve shows the observation peak, not the breeding calendar.

vocalizations.song.note: Wikipedia: song is a series of musical see notes. Season, time windows and cooldown are judgement.

vocalizations.chip.note: Wikipedia: call is a soft chip. Its alarm role is judgement.

behavior.note: Species-local program bt-canopy-warbler-v1 (behavior.json): the shared perching-songbird program makes food gait 'hop'. Flycatching and gleaning in foliage are represented as a 'fly' food action. Nest months 5-7 and the chip alarm are judgement.

look.note: Judgement. Breeding male palette from Wikipedia (black upperparts, orange wing patches, white underparts). Only the wing outer patches are coloured; the tail patches and orange breast sides are not modelled. Not checked in the previewer.

activity.US.note: US curve from GBIF occurrence counts (CC0 and CC BY 4.0 records), effort-corrected by the Aves baseline. iNaturalist (7 records) was not usable.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Judgement: the redstart roosts in shrub and bush cover; Wikipedia describes scrub and bush nesting only.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Wikipedia: eggs incubated 10-13 days; young fledge after 9 days in the nest and may stay with a parent up to 3 weeks.
